items.title: Geometric reducedness at a point may be checked after an arbitrary field extension
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section on geometrically reduced schemes

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that geometric reducedness of X over k at a point x is equivalent to geometric reducedness of the base change X_{k'} at every point x' over x, for an arbitrary field extension k'/k, and deduces the global statement (statement lines 492-502). The forward direction is by definition; the converse cannot be done by a single base change, because the definition tests all field extensions, so the proof replaces that by the finite purely inseparable ones and compares each of them with k' over a common extension k''', where the resulting local ring map is flat and local, hence faithfully flat, allowing reducedness to descend (proof lines 509-519). The two reduction devices, the finite inseparable criterion and faithful flatness descent, are the content. The claim is H2.
